title: Graphing a Horizontally Shifted Square Root Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = sqrt(x + 4) by identifying its parent function, transformation, natural domain, range, and intercepts.

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Transformation
steps.explanation: The function y = sqrt(x + 4) is obtained from the standard square root graph y = sqrt(x) by replacing x with x + 4, which shifts the graph 4 units to the left.
steps.why: Replacing x with x + c (c > 0) translates a graph horizontally to the left by c units.

steps.title: Determine the Domain and Range
steps.explanation: The radicand x + 4 must be non-negative, giving domain [-4, infinity). Since the horizontal shift does not affect vertical outputs, the range remains [0, infinity).
steps.why: Horizontal translations shift the domain interval while leaving the range unchanged.

steps.title: Locate Key Points and Intercepts
steps.explanation: The curve starts at (-4, 0), crosses the y-axis at (0, 2), and rises concavely to the right through (5, 3).
steps.why: Evaluating y(-4) = 0 and y(0) = 2 anchors the starting endpoint and y-axis crossing.
